title: Tate twists are well defined and locally free of rank one
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\cO_E$, and an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ containing $E$. Let $X$ be a scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible, and let $\mu_{\ell^n,X}$ be the sheaf of
$\ell^n$th roots of unity [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf], with transition maps
$\mu_{\ell^{n+1},X}\to\mu_{\ell^n,X}$, $u\mapsto u^\ell$. For every finite commutative ring $A$ and integer $r\geq1$ with $\ell^rA=0$, write $A_X$ for its constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Put $A_X(1)=\mu_{\ell^r,X}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/\ell^r)_X}A_X$, with sheaf tensor as in [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Interpret the coefficient objects and twists for $\cO_E$, $E$, and $\Qlb$ using [def-coefficient-twists-detailed].

1. There is a pro-étale cover $\widetilde X\to X$ and a compatible system
   $(\zeta_n)_{n\ge1}$, $\zeta_n\in\mu_{\ell^n,X}(\widetilde X)$, $\zeta_{n+1}^\ell=\zeta_n$,
   such that each $\zeta_n$ generates: $(\mathbf Z/\ell^n)_{\widetilde X}\to\mu_{\ell^n,\widetilde X}$,
   $a\mapsto\zeta_n^a$, is an isomorphism.
2. For $r'\ge r$, the Kummer map
   $\mu_{\ell^{r'},X}\to\mu_{\ell^r,X}$, $u\mapsto u^{\ell^{r'-r}}$, induces an isomorphism
   $\mu_{\ell^{r'},X}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^{r'}}A_X\cong\mu_{\ell^r,X}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^r}A_X$;
   so $A_X(1)$ is independent of $r$ up to canonical isomorphism.
3. For $\Lambda\in\{A,\cO_E,E,\Qlb\}$, the sheaf $\Lambda_X(1)$ is an invertible
   $\Lambda_X$-module: on $\widetilde X$ it is isomorphic to $\Lambda_{\widetilde X}$. Hence
   so are $\Lambda_X(d)$ and $\Lambda_X(-d)$ for $d\ge0$, and
   $\Lambda_X(d)\otimes\Lambda_X(-d)\cong\Lambda_X$. The functor $K\mapsto K(d)$ is an autoequivalence, with inverse $K\mapsto K(-d)$, on each coefficient category defined in [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]: $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},A)$ and the bounded constructible categories for $\cO_E$, $E$, and $\Qlb$.

proof.text: [lem-poincare-compatible-primitive-roots] trivializes the root diagram, transitions included, on one pro-étale covering family $(U_i)$; put $\widetilde X=\coprod_iU_i$, a pro-étale cover whose sections are families of sections. Images of $1$ give $\zeta_n$ with $\zeta_{n+1}^\ell=\zeta_n$; an abelian map killed by $\ell^n$ is residue-linear. Its inverse limit [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit] trivializes $T=\varprojlim\mu_{\ell^n}$ on that cover.

The Kummer map sends $\zeta_{r\prime}\otimes a$ to $\zeta_r\otimes a$, hence is the identity in the two $A$-bases [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Local inverses glue uniquely ($u=ufv=v$). Multiplying transition exponents gives canonical level independence.

Clause 3 of [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free] gives $L_E=T\otimes_{\widehat{\mathbf Z}_{\ell,X}}R_E$. Restrict tensors [lem-sfb-localized-site-tensor-restriction]: $e\otimes a\mapsto a$ trivializes every integral first line on the root cover.

Identify the continuous coefficient ring by [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit], then invert $\ell$ [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-invert-ell]. The same presentations at finite stages give the rational and $\Qlb$ lines [def-coefficient-twists-detailed].

source.place: Proof (3), rational and common-stage first lines

proof.text: [lem-weil-signed-line-tensor-equivalence] gives signed rank-one lines and opposite tensor inverses. In a local basis $p$, evaluation is $(ap)\otimes(bp^\vee)\mapsto ab$, inverse $a\mapsto(ap)\otimes p^\vee$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. These glue, including the unit at degree zero.
Apply [lem-pur-line-unbounded-derived-tensor] to each signed line. Its exact termwise model is derived tensor, and opposite evaluations give inverse functors on all of $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$.

source.place: Proof (3), final sentence, unbounded finite category

proof.text: Clause 3 of [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free] supplies finite locally constant reductions of $L_E$. Apply [lem-pur-integral-line-reduction-restriction]: the completed signed twists preserve completeness, constructibility and one uniform interval; their evaluations restrict.

The integral inverse pair is exact, $\mathcal O_E$-linear and inverse by step 6 and preserves $D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ by step 7. [lem-weil-twist-rationalization] therefore gives the specified rational inverse pair.

For $E\subset F$ use $(t\otimes a)\otimes b\mapsto t\otimes ab$ and inverse $t\otimes b\mapsto(t\otimes1)\otimes b$ [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed]. For the strict quotient-tower scalar extension [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], [lem-pur-completed-line-tensor-coherence] gives normalized signed scalar comparisons, tower laws and evaluation compatibility. For $E=F$ the map is multiplication, and both tower composites send $((t\otimes a)\otimes b)\otimes c$ to $t\otimes abc$: these are the hypotheses on $b_{ji}$ there.

[lem-sbc-coherent-pair-functor-descent] descends this normalized rational inverse pair and its evaluations to the common-stage category [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Thus the prescribed opposite twists are inverse also at $\Qlb$.

source.place: Proof (3), final sentence, common-stage inverse pair
